status: completed finite pass; manual-connected mechanics and bounded native engine recovery

chains.title: Annual preparation changes the coming year
chains.evidence_level: shipped manual semantics; native time-counter support separately qualified

sources.section: Forecasts and Omens; Allocating Magic; The Clan Ring

chains.prerequisite: Year-end rituals renew a limited magic budget; clan type and religious diversity on the ring change category capacity.
chains.decision: Read forecast and allocate crops, herds, health or other categories, retaining emergency reserve if desired.
chains.spend_state_change: Magic committed to categories augments next-year actions; crop rituals combine with blessings rather than replacing them.
chains.time_absence: Planting occurs in Sea season and harvesting in Earth season; annual forecast precedes decisions whose effects arrive later.
chains.downstream: Healthy labor, land, crops and magic together determine food; food surplus supports trade or gifts.
chains.failure_aftermath: Insufficient seasonal food prompts warnings; slaughter buys time at herd cost. Distant relief missions can arrive too late. Ignoring divine information has consequences according to the manual, but exact penalties were not decoded.
chains.inference: A forecast is useful because it precedes a resource commitment and offers different responses, rather than adding a flavor line.

chains.title: A leader leaving changes both missions and home capability

sources.section: Choosing Your Clan Ring; The Warleader
Choosing Your Emissary; Choosing an Escort

chains.prerequisite: Ring membership, skill and religion affect leadership functions and mission success.
chains.decision: Send a skilled ring member as envoy with gifts and escorts, or keep that person at home.
chains.spend_state_change: Gifts use goods/cattle; escorts remove working or fighting people from home. Ring members perform better on missions than outsiders.
chains.time_absence: Distant missions may take at least a season. Travelers are temporarily subtracted from population, so annual recap can misleadingly look like demographic loss.
chains.downstream: Another member replaces an absent warleader; temporary absence weakens annual rituals while permanent vacancy also harms magic and mood.
chains.failure_aftermath: Bandits and feuding neighbors threaten unguarded parties; people return to the available population only if they survive.
chains.inference: A person should be a scarce capability with location and availability, rather than a permanent bonus detached from their whereabouts.

chains.title: Growing children sustain work and replace aging leaders
chains.evidence_level: shipped manual semantics with bounded native aging confirmation

sources.section: Leader Skills; Choosing Your Clan Ring

chains.prerequisite: Children consume food before contributing adult labor; health determines who can work or advise.
chains.decision: Keep sufficient producers for dependents and reorganize when leaders die, become wounded or improve.
chains.spend_state_change: Children become farmers or nobles after fifteen years according to the manual; hunters teach children their occupation. New leaders emerge as old leaders disappear.
chains.time_absence: This is a multi-year production and capability pipeline; skill growth can justify later promotion.
chains.downstream: Leader skills influence agriculture, negotiation, battle and ritual success; successor composition therefore changes ordinary clan operations.
chains.failure_aftermath: Too many dependent children compared with farmers increases starvation risk; sickness makes old-age/starvation deaths more likely and removes workers from tasks.

native_support.observed: Increments a 16-bit age field; branches at age 51 into a different randomized skill-update path. Floating-point skill slots are read/modified.
native_support.limit: Exact development/decline rates and mortality formula were not reconstructed; do not import the threshold or odds into YAIR as design decisions.

chains.inference: Aging should redistribute useful capabilities and create succession pressure in roles the player already cares about.

chains.title: Gifts create debts with later political use

sources.section: Gift Giving; Ask for Favor; Feuds; Allies

chains.prerequisite: Neighbor relationships include public attitude, concealed commoner grievances, alliances, feuds and favor balance.
chains.decision: Send a substantial gift, collect a favor now, or keep the debt outstanding for influence later.
chains.spend_state_change: Favors net in one direction; a new opposing favor reduces debt rather than creating two simultaneous obligations. Large gifts can count as repayment.
chains.time_absence: Envoys travel; collecting food aid has delivery latency. Uncollected debt influences later negotiations.
chains.downstream: Allies can assist without prior debt; owed favors improve receptiveness in disputes; generosity can help end feuds.
chains.failure_aftermath: Small gifts can lower reputation; ending a feud may upset the player clan; friendly leader attitude does not eliminate commoner grievances or future feuds.
chains.inference: Use signed obligation balances and separate relationship layers so polite surface interactions do not erase history.

chains.title: Recruitment solves shortages with delayed social consequences

sources.section: Farmers; Weaponthanes; The Clan Mood; Farmer Morale and Weaponthane Morale

chains.prerequisite: Cultivated land needs healthy labor; military recruitment needs goods and horses.
chains.decision: Recruit newcomers generously, reassign hunters, or reduce demanding land use.
chains.spend_state_change: Warrior recruitment is bounded by welcoming gifts and mounts; more workers can support land but generous newcomer treatment can offend existing farmers.
chains.time_absence: Farmer recruitment resolves after one or two seasons; hunters already provide food, exploration and detection support, so reassignment has opportunity cost.
chains.downstream: Professional morale differs from whole-clan mood. Bad mood makes small disputes escalate and repeated poor leadership can become rebellion.
chains.failure_aftermath: Luring another clan’s workers harms relations; excessive cultivated acreage overworks farmers, lowers productivity and increases dissatisfaction. Dismissing warriors may increase banditry.
chains.inference: Delayed recruitment is an event chain with source, arrival and acceptance, rather than an instant headcount purchase.

chains.title: Events run through conditions, responses and delayed state
chains.evidence_level: bounded native disassembly and structural data decode

sources.path: King of Dragon Pass.app/Contents/Resources/King of Dragon Pass.s86

sources.section: Header and 1760 indexed record boundaries; individual opcode semantics not decoded

chains.prerequisite: Scene eligibility can be a special sentinel or an OSL VM program; narrative payload is custom indexed bytecode, not JSON or managed C#.
chains.decision: Active response lookup precedes running the response program.
chains.spend_state_change: DoResponse clears active-response flag, executes COSL::Run at the response offset and calls CheckResult. CheckResult routes advice, queued outcome or completed state to the current scene.
chains.time_absence: AdvanceYear decrements only positive entries in a scene counter array; semantic labels of those counters remain unresolved. The manual independently describes delayed consequences and future events.
chains.downstream: Read loads scene record and invokes VM; yearly saga omits minor details and stores the omen for later reference. Manual says annual saves precede Sacred Time.
chains.failure_aftermath: COSL bounds execution at 0x43e3 words and recognizes stop command 0x400. Do not infer every event’s conditions or cost from dispatcher structure.
chains.inference: Separate eligible scene, committed response, scheduled aftermath and compact remembered history; do not persist every presentation string.

global_limits: No game launch or user saves read.
Five mechanic chains are semantics documented by installed manual, not complete per-scene source reconstruction.
1760 record boundaries decoded and validated, but OSL opcode/variable mapping and arbitrary scene-specific choices/probabilities remain unread.
Native disassembly is executable instruction recovery, not original C++ source or gameplay acceptance.
